issues_detected.description: keywords lists only four broad terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice), below the five-keyword threshold and covering neither the acoustic modalities (speech, cough, breathing), the disease cohorts (voice disorders, Parkinson's/neurodegenerative, mood and psychiatric, respiratory), nor the methods or formats (spectrogram, MFCC, BIDS, Parquet) that a searcher would use. The rich description is not compensated for at the index level.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add keywords for modality (speech, cough, respiratory sound), cohort conditions, method terms (acoustic biomarker, MFCC, spectrogram, phonetic posteriorgram) and standards (BIDS, Parquet).

issues_detected.description: variables documents only four columns (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames), all from the Parquet feature files, while the release also distributes phenotype tables covering confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaires and task metadata. The join keys are defined and flagged with is_identifier, but column-level metadata for the tabular phenotype data is delegated entirely to external JSON data dictionaries.
issues_detected.recommendation: Extend variables with the principal phenotype table columns, or record a pointer to the published JSON data dictionaries as a variable-metadata resource with its URL.

issues_detected.description: No `publisher` slot is populated and no `download_url` slot is populated. The publishing platform (PhysioNet, MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology) and the access endpoints are nonetheless stated unambiguously in citation, page, maintainers, third_party_sharing and distribution_formats.access_urls, and the record states explicitly and accurately that no direct file endpoint is published because PhysioNet gates the files behind credentialing.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate `publisher` with PhysioNet and `download_url` with the credentialed-access endpoint (or repeat the landing page there) so platform and retrieval are machine-readable from their canonical slots.

issues_detected.description: source_caveats discloses a grant-identifier rendering '3Tf-OTOD03272001S2' taken from a documentation footer, which matches no NIH grant-number pattern. The record does not assert it as the award; the canonical renderings it records in funders.grants (OT2OD032720, 3OT2OD032720-01S1) are both well formed NIH Other Transaction numbers.
issues_detected.recommendation: Retain the disclosure but mark the footer rendering explicitly as a transcription artifact of OT2OD032720 so downstream parsers do not treat it as an award identifier.

issues_detected.description: collection_timeframes states a 12-month collection period while the same field records that the IRB protocol describes a four-year phased study with pilot collection from November 2023 still running in November 2024. The conflict is surfaced by the record itself in source_caveats with a stated source-ranking rationale rather than silently resolved.
issues_detected.recommendation: If the 12 months denote the window for the released version specifically, state the start and end dates so the subset relationship to the wider study period is explicit.

issues_detected.description: confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present is false, asserting no legally privileged or doctor-patient confidential content, while regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance records that the underlying data are covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality assertable against subpoenas. The tension is disclosed in confidential_elements.source_caveats; the two claims are reconcilable because the released feature set excludes the raw audio and clinical narrative, but the false flag reads more absolutely than the governance record supports.
issues_detected.recommendation: Scope the false flag to the registered-access feature release and note the Certificate of Confidentiality as applying to the controlled-access holdings.

issues_detected.description: The description lists pediatric voice and speech disorders among the five cohort categories of the collection, while this record is the adult dataset (833 adult participants) and routes the pediatric cohort to a separate related dataset. subpopulations resolves the tension ('the adult dataset contains adult participants only'), but the opening description could be read as claiming pediatric coverage in this release.
issues_detected.recommendation: Qualify the cohort list in the description to distinguish the consortium-wide protocol from the contents of this adult release.

issues_detected.description: is_tabular is not set, data_protection_impacts is absent (no formal DPIA is recorded even though a two-tier access model and an ethics-working-group memorandum are), imputation_protocols is absent (the no-imputation decision is stated in missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy instead), and was_derived_from is unused (provenance is carried by raw_data_sources and preprocessing_strategies).
issues_detected.recommendation: Set is_tabular for the TSV phenotype tables, record the ethics memorandum as a data_protection_impacts entry, and mirror the no-imputation statement into imputation_protocols.

semantic_insights: DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 uses the PhysioNet prefix 10.13026, consistent with the stated host, the landing page physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ and the citation; every version-specific DOI in version_access (249v-w155, k81f-qr68, 8xbn-nq66, 37yb-1t42) and both related-dataset DOIs share that prefix, and the Health Data Nexus release correctly carries a different prefix (10.57764).

The record distinguishes a version-specific identifier (id/doi = 10.13026/8xbn-nq66) from a version-agnostic latest-version DOI (10.13026/37yb-1t42) and states which referent the datasheet describes — a distinction most datasheets collapse.
RRID:SCR_007345 in the citation is a well-formed SCR resource identifier; it identifies the PhysioNet platform rather than the dataset, which is the correct use in a PhysioNet citation.

Grant numbers OT2OD032720 and 3OT2OD032720-01S1 match NIH structure (activity code OT2, institute OD, six-digit serial, supplement suffix) and the funder named is the NIH Common Fund, the correct administering body for a Bridge2AI OT2 award.

Human-subjects logic holds end to end: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by named IRBs (USF single IRB; SickKids REB for the pediatric arm), by a detailed informed_consent block with four consent modalities and a withdrawal mechanism, by participant_compensation with amounts and caps, and by at_risk_populations with assent and guardian-permission procedures.

Deidentification is internally coherent and unusually candid: HIPAA Safe Harbor plus removal of indirect and highly sensitive fields, an itemized identifiers_removed list, date rebasing, and an explicit statement that k-anonymity with k>=2 is NOT achieved — a negative disclosure that most records omit.

The deidentification method is appropriate to the data type and is reconciled with residual risk: participant_privacy.reidentification_risk states that voice is inherently identifying, which is given as the stated reason raw audio is withheld from the registered-access release and routed through DACO controlled access on Synapse.

The two-tier access model is consistent across license_and_use_terms, regulatory_restrictions, data_governance, raw_data_sources.access_details and distribution_formats: the same registered/controlled split is described from five directions without contradiction.

Prohibited_uses prohibits re-identification attempts, matching the re-identification risk assessment; prohibited_uses also prohibits IP-based obstruction of access, matching ip_restrictions — restrictiveness is aligned with the stated ethical risks rather than boilerplate.

Temporal ordering is coherent: collection from 2023, releases from November 2024 (Health Data Nexus v1.0) through 1 May 2026 (v3.1.0), with `issued` 2026-05-01 matching the v3.1.0 release date given in distribution_dates.

known_biases uses taxonomy-style bias_type values (representation_bias, selection_bias, measurement_bias, annotation_bias) and each is causally grounded in a collection fact recorded elsewhere — the site/device confound in collection_mechanisms, the single-labeler scheme in labeling_strategies.annotations_per_item=1.

Processing software is named at the level of the transformation it performed: b2aiprep for organization and Parquet conversion, senselab for audio processing, sparc for articulatory traces, openSMILE/Parselmouth/Praat for acoustic and phonetic features, ppgs for posteriorgrams, Whisper Large for transcription — with an explicit caveat that the off-the-shelf transcription model was not audited.

The record carries an unusual discipline of source-conflict disclosure: enrollment target, consortium size, recording counts, investigator name spellings, grant renderings and the free-speech transcript question are each recorded with the competing sources and the ranking rationale, rather than presented as settled.

overall_score.comparability_note: No sub-element was excluded, so the adjusted and fixed bases coincide at 50. Comparisons with other records must name any item identities whose applicability differs, not only the excluded point totals.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66; doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; citation includes RRID:SCR_007345; version_access.version_details lists 10.13026/249v-w155 (v1.1), 10.13026/k81f-qr68 (v3.0.0), 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 (v3.1.0), 10.13026/37yb-1t42 (latest), 10.57764/qb6h-em84 (Health Data Nexus v1.0)
sub_elements.quality_note: A version-specific DOI is provided and is distinguished from the version-agnostic latest-version DOI, with per-version DOIs enumerated. Identification is unambiguous as to referent.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: DOI matches 10.XXXX/ pattern; prefix 10.13026 is the PhysioNet registrant prefix and matches the stated host and landing page. RRID:SCR_007345 is well-formed SCR syntax and correctly denotes the PhysioNet resource within the citation rather than the dataset.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description (~1,900 characters) covering cohorts, protocol, participant count (833 across five North American sites), released feature types, formats, the raw-audio exclusion and the consortium AI-readiness self-assessment scores
sub_elements.quality_note: Far beyond the 200-character threshold, and specific rather than promotional: it names what is in the public release (derived features, phenotype tables) and what is not (raw recordings), which is the single most consequential fact for a prospective user.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Description content is semantically appropriate for a clinical voice-biomarker dataset and is consistent with instances (833 participants), distribution_formats (Parquet/TSV) and raw_data_sources (audio under controlled access).

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: [health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice]
sub_elements.quality_note: Only four keywords, all broad. None names a modality beyond voice (speech, cough, breathing), a cohort condition, a method or feature type, or a standard. A searcher looking for 'Parkinson', 'dysphonia', 'spectrogram' or 'BIDS' would not reach this record through its tags, so the indexing layer does not carry the specificity the description does.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Below the five-keyword threshold and lacking domain, method and condition coverage; terms are individually accurate but non-discriminating.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; distribution_formats.access_urls repeat the landing page and give https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/ for controlled-access audio; external_resources link https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/
sub_elements.quality_note: A version-pinned landing page on the hosting platform, plus a distinct endpoint for the controlled-access tier and a documentation site. Resource structure is expressed through distribution_formats and external_resources rather than a nested `resources` slot.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: URLs are well-formed and the domains are plausible and consistent with the named hosts (PhysioNet, Synapse/Sage, project documentation site).

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: relationship_type is_supplemented_by -> doi:10.13026/h995-bt35 (Bridge2AI-Voice Pediatric Dataset, 23,533 recordings from 300 participants aged 2-18); relationship_type is_new_version_of -> doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84 (v1.0 on Health Data Nexus)
sub_elements.quality_note: Two typed relationships with resolvable DOIs and substantive descriptions that explain why each companion exists (separate REB approval and protocol for the pediatric arm; a prior host for the first release). parent_datasets is unused, but the relational structure is expressed.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship types are used semantically correctly: the pediatric release is a sibling collection rather than a version, and the Health Data Nexus release is correctly typed as a prior version with a different registrant prefix.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: general_research_use; license_terms describing the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, mandatory credentialing and signature of the Registered Access Agreement, permitted duplication, prohibition on sale, no fees; ip_restrictions.restrictions stating no transfer of IP, recipients' rights over downstream discoveries, and that no third party has imposed IP-based restrictions
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the access policy and the IP position are stated in operational terms a legal reviewer could act on, including the Fort Lauderdale Agreement commitment and the explicit no-fee statement.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: License restrictiveness is proportionate to the stated sensitivity (registered access for features, controlled for audio) and does not contradict the general_research_use permission code.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; regulatory_restrictions: 'No export controls or other regulatory restrictions apply'; other_compliance: Certificate of Confidentiality, safeguards requirement, five-business-day breach reporting, PhysioNet requirements; data_governance.committee_name: Bridge2AI-Voice Data Access Compliance Office (DACO) with contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org in access_review_process and stewardship_roles
sub_elements.quality_note: Classification, HIPAA status, an affirmative statement that export controls do not apply, additional compliance obligations and a reachable governance contact are all present. The contact sits in access_review_process/stewardship_roles prose rather than a dedicated committee_contact slot, but is unambiguous.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: HIPAA-compliant status is consistent with the Safe Harbor method in is_deidentified; the 'restricted' classification is consistent with credentialed access and with the Certificate of Confidentiality. Note the tension between confidential_elements_present=false and the Certificate, disclosed by the record itself.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats.access_urls: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; notes: 'No direct download URL is published: the PhysioNet files are gated behind credentialing and a signed data use agreement'; data_governance.access_review_process gives the step-by-step route (PhysioNet registration and identity confirmation; DACO request form, DUA, institutionally signed DUTA); DACO@b2ai-voice.org for enquiries
sub_elements.quality_note: The `download_url` slot is empty, but the sub-element admits platform access instructions and those are exceptionally complete: two platform endpoints, the credentialing path for each tier, and a named office with an email. The record also explains truthfully why no file endpoint exists, which is more useful than a link that would fail behind the gate.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: URLs well-formed; the absence of a direct endpoint is consistent with the registered/controlled access model asserted elsewhere rather than an omission.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: (1) Apache Parquet holding spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, pitch, SPARC articulatory estimates, loudness, periodicity, phonetic posteriorgrams and a per-recording metadata file; (2) tab-separated values with accompanying JSON data dictionaries holding static features, audio quality metrics and phenotype tables; (3) WAV with JSON sidecars organized per BIDS, controlled access only
sub_elements.quality_note: Formats are named per tier and mapped to the specific contents each carries, so a user can tell which artifact answers which question. MIME types and byte sizes are not given.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Parquet, TSV+JSON and WAV+BIDS sidecars are appropriate and standard choices for dense audio features, phenotype tables and raw audio respectively; format assignment matches content type in each case.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets (pediatric companion; Health Data Nexus v1.0) plus six external_resources: eipm/bridge2ai-redcap (GitHub + Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.12760724, MIT), sensein/b2aiprep (Apache-2.0), sensein/senselab, eipm/bridge2ai-docs (GitHub + Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.13834653, MIT), Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles, and the Scholars training program at b2aivoicescholars.org
sub_elements.quality_note: Resources are linked with URLs, licenses and archival flags, and the record marks where a URL was not available in the source (the FHIR profiles) rather than fabricating one.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Zenodo DOIs carry the correct 10.5281 prefix; repository URLs and licenses are internally consistent (MIT for documentation/REDCap artifacts, Apache-2.0 for the processing library).

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on external evidence: distribution_formats is populated with three tiers; page https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ is an accessible dataset landing page; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission=general_research_use explicitly permits research reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: general_research_use; license_terms permit use by approved credentialed users for commercial and non-commercial research, permit duplication as required for the approved project, and state 'There are no fees associated with these restrictions'; intended_uses.usage_notes confirm research use by Authorized Researchers
sub_elements.quality_note: Reuse is affirmatively permitted with the conditions, the permitted scope and the cost position all stated. The restrictions that remain (no sale, no re-identification, no IP obstruction) are enumerated rather than left to a linked document.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: License permissiveness is consistent with prohibited_uses and ip_restrictions; no contradiction between the general_research_use code and the registered-access gating.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence: distribution_formats populated, landing page accessible, license permits reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: 'Apache Parquet, an open-source column-oriented data file format'; 'Tab-separated values with accompanying JSON data dictionaries'; 'WAV audio files with accompanying JSON sidecars, organized per the Brain Imaging Data Structure'; conforms_to: Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0
sub_elements.quality_note: All three tiers use open, widely tooled formats, and the audio tier is organized under a named community layout standard with a pinned version. Character encoding of the TSV files is not stated.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Format choices are semantically appropriate to the data they carry; the Parquet choice is consistent with the dense frame-level features described in preprocessing_strategies (50 Hz articulatory traces, 100 Hz posteriorgrams).

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence: distribution_formats populated, landing page accessible, license permits reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; preprocessing_strategies describe conversion of audio and questionnaire data to BIDS v1.9.0, with pediatric ReproSchema data transformed to REDCap format first; external_resources list Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is claimed at three levels — data layout (BIDS, version-pinned), metadata schema (the Bridge2AI data-sheets schema with a resolvable w3id URI and class), and a clinical interoperability profile (FHIR) — and the BIDS claim is backed by a described conversion step rather than asserted.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: BIDS is used correctly for the audio/derivative layout; the version pin (1.9.0) is a real BIDS release line and is consistent between conforms_to and preprocessing_strategies.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence: distribution_formats populated, landing page accessible, license permits reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: variables: participant_id (identifier, is_identifier=true, 'present in every Parquet feature file and used to join the phenotype tables'), session_id (identifier, is_identifier=true, 'a participant may have more than one session'), task_name (categorical), n_frames (integer); distribution_formats note that TSV tables ship with accompanying JSON data dictionaries
sub_elements.quality_note: The two join keys that cross-dataset integration actually depends on are defined, flagged as identifiers, and their cardinality explained (multiple sessions per participant, echoed in relationships and missing_data_documentation). Coverage is nevertheless thin for a release containing demographic, diagnosis, enrollment and questionnaire tables, and the column-level detail for those is delegated to external dictionaries — a real weakness recorded in issues_detected, but not one that defeats this sub-element's integration purpose.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Identifier semantics are consistent across variables, relationships ('recordings are grouped by session') and missing_data_documentation ('more than one row per participant'); data_type assignments are appropriate.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses (research: model development, clinical research, pretraining/fine-tuning/benchmarking; cohort selection from phenotype questionnaire features); discouraged_uses (hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustment, surveillance; uses ignoring disorder/site/demographic skew); prohibited_uses (re-identification attempts; foreseeable harm or stigmatization; IP-based obstruction of access; sale of data; contacting subjects without IRB approval, provider approval and consent)
sub_elements.quality_note: All three registers are populated, each with a stated reason rather than a bare rule, and the discouraged/prohibited items map onto specific risks named elsewhere in the record (re-identification risk, demographic skew). This is usable governance guidance, not boilerplate.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Guidance is coherent with the license and with the ethics disclosures; the prohibition on re-identification directly answers participant_privacy.reidentification_risk.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition met on Element 1 and Element 8 evidence: description states participants were recruited at expert clinics on the basis of five disease cohort categories; collection_mechanisms (E8) describe an in-clinic tablet protocol administered to participants. The governance condition is independently met: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level=restricted (E2) is an applying constraint.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: University of South Florida IRB (approved the Voice Data Acquisition protocol and the sharing of resulting data; US sites brought under single IRB), Research Ethics Board of The Hospital for Sick Children (pediatric cohort), Bridge2AI-Voice ethics working group (identified sensitive fields for removal and produced a published memorandum justifying controlled access to raw voice); human_subject_research.irb_approval and ethics_review_board name the same bodies; regulatory_compliance notes NIH STRIDES hosting agreements and that no data monitoring committee was required
sub_elements.quality_note: Oversight is named at institution level, covers both the US single-IRB structure and separate Canadian REB approvals, and extends to an ethics body that made a specific, auditable decision about what was withheld. No formal DPIA is recorded under data_protection_impacts, but the ethics memorandum plus the risk assessment in participant_privacy serve the equivalent function.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by populated ethics review. Reviewing bodies are plausible for the named collection sites (USF as lead, SickKids for the pediatric arm).

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition met on E1 description (clinic-recruited participants, disease cohorts) and E8 collection_mechanisms (in-clinic protocol with participants); governance condition independently met by confidentiality_level=restricted (E2).
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.method: 'HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification, supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers and of non-identifying but highly sensitive fields, and by exclusion of the raw audio'; identifiers_removed itemizes the Safe Harbor set plus state/province, household composition, income, mental health status and traumatic life experiences, and all raw voice data; deidentification_details: dates rebased to integers, geography generalized, narrative text removed, transcripts reviewed and recordings with identifying content or external voices removed, 'K-anonymization with k of 2 or more is not achieved'
sub_elements.quality_note: A named standard, an itemized removal list, the specific transformations applied, and an explicit statement of the residual weakness. The negative disclosure about k-anonymity is the kind of statement that makes the rest of the block credible.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Method is appropriate to the data type: Safe Harbor addresses the phenotype tables, and the additional exclusion of raw audio addresses the biometric residual that Safe Harbor does not cover — consistent with participant_privacy.reidentification_risk and with sensitive_elements.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Participant condition met on E1/E8 evidence: description references research participants recruited in clinics; collection_mechanisms (E8) describe administration of the protocol to participants. Applicability here rests on the existence of participants, not on any governance structure.
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy.anonymization_method (Safe Harbor identifiers plus indirect and sensitive fields, raw audio excluded); privacy_techniques (two-tier registered/controlled access model plus transcript review to remove recordings with identifying content or non-consented voices); reidentification_risk ('K-anonymization with k of 2 or more is not achieved... each person's voice is unique to them and re-identification by voice cannot be entirely excluded, which is the reason raw audio is disseminated only under controlled access'); data_linkage (internal study numbers; linking tables held behind institutional access controls, not shared between sites)
sub_elements.quality_note: The risk assessment is explicit, quantitative where it can be, and directly tied to the mitigation it motivates. Linkage-key custody is described at the level of who holds what and where, which is what a privacy reviewer needs.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistency check passes: risk is assessed and mitigations are proportionate. The residual-risk statement reconciles with is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present=false, which concerns direct identifiers in the released tables rather than biometric uniqueness in withheld audio.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Participant condition met on E1/E8 evidence: clinic-recruited research participants in the description; collection_mechanisms (E8) describe a participant-administered protocol.
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent.consent_obtained=true; consent_type lists four modalities (paper signature, in-app electronic consent, REDCap survey consent, video consent in which the participant reads a statement aloud so acoustic data can be verified as belonging to the consented individual); consent_scope covers collection and use, external sharing of non-directly-identifying data, registered-access public release and controlled-access release, plus EHR access for gold-standard validation; consent_documentation (REDCap storage, five-year minimum retention, re-consent before each subsequent longitudinal collection); withdrawal_mechanism; plus collection_consents, collection_notifications and consent_revocations
sub_elements.quality_note: Consent is documented at the level of mechanism, scope, storage and revocation, and the scope explicitly anticipates the two-tier release model this datasheet describes — so the release is traceable to what participants agreed to. The withdrawal limit (data retained if withdrawal follows completed collection) is stated plainly rather than glossed.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistency check passes: IRB approval and consent procedures are both present, as the cross-field rule requires. The video-consent modality is semantically coherent with the acoustic subject matter.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Participant condition met on E1/E8 evidence: description references participants with neurological, neurodegenerative and psychiatric conditions recruited in clinics; collection_mechanisms (E8) describe in-clinic administration.
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included=true; special_protections (enrollment of participants with cognitive impairment, dementia and psychiatric conditions; consent by trained staff with comprehension teach-back; voluntariness with no effect on medical care; children's research checklist appended to the protocol); guardian_consent (one parent or guardian permitted given minimal risk); assent_procedures (documented verbal assent, waived below roughly seven years); participant_compensation (electronic gift cards, USD 40 under 90 minutes, USD 80 over, maximum three sessions and USD 120 total, adults only, with a caveat that the feasibility study offered no incentive)
sub_elements.quality_note: Both halves are substantive: the protections are specific to the named vulnerabilities (comprehension teach-back for cognitive impairment; assent rules keyed to developmental capacity), and compensation is given with amounts, caps and the rationale, including the adult-only restriction.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Compensation amounts are plausible and non-coercive for the stated session burden; the adult-only compensation policy is consistent with the pediatric cohort being released separately.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations entry 1: elements present, identified by age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status in the demographics table, with distribution noting skews by disorder category, site and demographics and that groups with less trust in the medical system or less proximity to sites were less likely to be recruited; entry 2: the five disease cohort categories plus controls, with the note that public releases do not contain an equal distribution and that the adult dataset contains adults only
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the demographic axes and the clinical strata are described, and each carries an honest distribution statement rather than a claim of balance. Inclusion criteria are further given in sampling_strategies.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Subpopulation structure is consistent with known_biases (representation and selection bias) and with the separate pediatric release.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances: instance_type 'research participant', counts: 833; description: 'Version 3.1.0 contains data for 833 participants across five North American sites'; source_caveats records the per-feature recording counts from the PhysioNet page (32,522 pitch series, 29,278 spectrograms, 29,289 phonetic posteriorgram files) against the documentation's approximate 61,937 figure
sub_elements.quality_note: A specific participant count is given and reconciled with the landing page. The recording-level instance carries no single count, but the record explains why — the release reports per-feature counts, not one recording total — and reproduces those figures rather than inventing an aggregate.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: 833 is consistent between description, instances and the cited source; the caveat resolves a genuine conflict between two sources with a stated ranking rule.

strengths: Ethics documentation is complete across all five sub-elements and internally coherent: named IRBs and REBs, four consent modalities with scope that explicitly anticipates the two-tier release, itemized Safe Harbor deidentification, an explicit re-identification risk assessment that states k-anonymity is not achieved, and vulnerable-population protections keyed to the specific vulnerabilities enrolled.

Preprocessing is specified at reproducible parameter level — 16 kHz mono with Butterworth anti-aliasing, 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, 60 MFCCs, 50 Hz articulatory traces, 100 Hz posteriorgrams — with each feature family attributed to the named software that produced it (b2aiprep, sparc, openSMILE, Parselmouth/Praat, ppgs, Whisper Large).

Version and provenance tracking is exemplary: six releases enumerated with per-version DOIs, a version-agnostic latest DOI distinguished from the referent DOI, a support policy with its caveat, and per-version errata that name breaking changes such as renamed gold-standard variables and rearranged phenotype files.

Limitations and biases are disclosed with unusual candour, including four taxonomy-aligned bias types each grounded in a specific collection fact, the site/device/disease confound, single-labeler annotation, and the consortium's own failing AI-readiness criteria.

The record systematically discloses conflicts between its sources — collection window, enrollment target, consortium size, recording counts, grant renderings, investigator name spellings and the free-speech transcript question — each with the competing sources and the ranking rationale, so a reader can audit the choices rather than inherit them.
weaknesses: Keywords are reduced to four broad terms that carry none of the specificity of the description: no modality beyond voice, no cohort condition, no method or standard. The record is far more discoverable by reading than by searching.

Variable metadata covers only four Parquet columns while the release distributes demographic, diagnosis, enrollment, confounder and questionnaire tables whose column semantics are delegated entirely to external JSON data dictionaries that are not themselves linked.

Canonical slots are left empty where the information exists in prose: `publisher` (PhysioNet), `download_url`, `is_tabular`, `data_protection_impacts`, `imputation_protocols`, `was_derived_from` and `data_governance.committee_contact`. Machine consumers reading those paths would find nothing.

Two internal tensions remain unresolved even though both are disclosed: the 12-month collection window against the four-year IRB study period, and confidential_elements_present=false against a Certificate of Confidentiality covering the underlying data.

Feature-extraction software is named but not version-pinned (openSMILE, Praat, sparc, ppgs, Whisper Large), which limits exact reproducibility of the released features despite the parameter-level detail.
recommendations: Expand keywords to at least a dozen terms spanning modality (speech, cough, breathing), cohort conditions (dysphonia, Parkinson's disease, depression, asthma), methods (acoustic biomarker, MFCC, spectrogram, phonetic posteriorgram) and standards (BIDS, Parquet, FHIR).
Extend `variables` to the principal phenotype table columns, or add the published JSON data dictionaries as linked external_resources so column-level semantics are reachable from the datasheet.

Populate the empty canonical slots with information the record already contains: publisher=PhysioNet, download_url for the credentialed endpoint, is_tabular for the TSV tables, the ethics working group memorandum under data_protection_impacts, the no-imputation decision under imputation_protocols, and DACO@b2ai-voice.org under data_governance.committee_contact.

Resolve the two disclosed tensions: give explicit start and end dates for the released version's collection window, and scope confidential_elements_present to the registered-access feature release while recording the Certificate of Confidentiality as applying to the controlled-access holdings.

Pin versions for the feature-extraction stack (b2aiprep, senselab, openSMILE, Praat/Parselmouth, sparc, ppgs, Whisper Large) so the released features can be regenerated exactly, and flag the footer grant rendering '3Tf-OTOD03272001S2' explicitly as a transcription artifact of OT2OD032720.
